To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tumor suppressor gene SMAD1 is silenced by hypermethylation in DLBCL, and that the pharmacological reactivation of SMAD1 by DAC sensitizes tumor cells to TGF-beta-induced apoptosis and reduces the tumor growth in DLBCL.
the tumor suppressive TGF-β/SMAD1 pathway is blocked at the epigenetic level in DLBCL and that the restoration of SMAD signaling through epigenetic therapy can reverse tumor growth.

pharmacological DNA demethyaltion restores SMAD1 and TGF-β/TGF-βRI/SMAD1 tumor suppressive signaling, and sensitizes DLBCL cells to TGFβ-induced apoptosis, which reduces tumor growth in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel treatment approaches in DLBCL.
the role of the epigenome in the pathogenesis of DLBCL and its potential for therapeutic intervention.
the identification of epigenetic alterations that drive the development of DLBCL and the development of new therapies that restore tumor suppressive TGF-β/SMAD signaling in this disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pharmacological DNA demethlation by DAC restores SMAD 1 expression and tumor-suppressive signaling in DLBCL.
the TGF-beta signaling pathway in DLBL is blocked by SMAD1 hypermethylation and the restoration of SMAD 1 expression by DAC sensitizes cells to apoptosis and reduces the tumor growth.

the TGFβ/SMAD1/S1PR2 signaling axis is a major tumor suppressor axis that is inappropriately repressed in a large proportion of patients with DLBCL and that pharmacological restoration of SMAD expression may have therapeutic potential in DLBCL patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TGFβ pathway is a tumor suppressor pathway in DLBCC and that its inactivation by epigenetic silencing is a key step in the pathogenesis of DLBCC and is a potential target for therapy.
we show that TGF-β/SMAD1/S1PR2 signaling is inactivated in DLBCL and that restoration of SMAD 1 expression by DAC is an effective treatment strategy.
S1PRs are a new class of tumor suppressors in DLBCL.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the epigenetic silencing of the TGF-ß/SMAD1 pathway in DLBCH is a major driver of lymphomagenesis and that the restoration of this pathway by pharmacological means can be a novel strategy in the treatment of this disease.
the epigenome of DLBCL can be pharmacologically targeted to restore TGF-β-mediated tumor suppression.
the TGFβ/SMAD1/S1PR2 axis is an essential tumor suppressive pathway in DLBCC that is frequently inactivated by hypermethylation.
